destination.name: Hawkesbury
destination.tagline: A river district on Sydney's north-west edge, built around the five Macquarie towns of 1811.
destination.description: The City of Hawkesbury covers the far north-west fringe of Greater Sydney along the Hawkesbury River, with Windsor and Richmond as its main towns. Governor Lachlan Macquarie established five towns here by 1811 (Windsor, Richmond, Castlereagh, Wilberforce and Pitt Town), and many early 19th-century buildings survive. Windsor, the fourth oldest place of British settlement on the Australian continent, is the base for the district's heritage buildings. National parks to the north and east add canoeing at Cattai and a post-war migrant camp at Scheyville.

goodToKnow.title: Flood-prone river
goodToKnow.detail: Windsor floods often; a horseshoe on the outside wall of the Macquarie Arms marks the 1867 flood peak.

goodToKnow.title: Park fees and hours
goodToKnow.detail: Cattai National Park charges $8 per vehicle per day, opens 8 AM to 8 PM from September to April and 8 AM to 6 PM from May to August, and has weekday closures from 12 to 23 October 2026.

goodToKnow.title: Check Scheyville first
goodToKnow.detail: Scheyville’s Longneck boardwalk is closed at the time of research; check NPWS alerts for the Longneck Lagoon walk before driving out.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} give mild weather for walking Windsor's historic streets and the park tracks, avoiding the long hot summers typical of Sydney's west.
